Subject: Inquiry from illustrator GEGYjiji — watercolor zine / consignment possibility

Dear UTRECHT team,

I have long admired how UTRECHT brings together artist books, zines, and illustrated works that sit quietly between fine art and everyday life, and I think my work may belong in that same conversation. I am GEGYjiji, a Chinese watercolor artist based in Tokyo, and in 2021 I published Colour Diary, a small illustration collection grown from a daily watercolor practice that documents domestic interiors, neighborhood light, and the quiet texture of city life — much of it observed here in Tokyo. My work has been shown in Tokyo most recently as part of Tide from China, a group exhibition at ACG_Labo in Harajuku in 2023, and I am now looking to place printed work or original pieces in spaces where that kind of attentive, intimate scale feels at home. I would love to explore whether a consignment arrangement or a small exhibition might be a possibility, and you are welcome to see more of my work on Instagram at @gegyjiji. Thank you very much for your time, and I hope to hear from you.

GEGYjiji

Subject: Submission Inquiry — 2026年美の起原展 / GEGYjiji (Watercolor Artist, Tokyo)

Dear 2026年美の起原展 Selection Committee,

I am writing to express my interest in submitting work to the 2026年美の起原展, an open call I understand welcomes painting and illustration in formats from 10 to 20号, with an emphasis on considered, atmospheric work across media. My name is GEGYjiji, a Chinese watercolor artist based in Tokyo, and my practice centers on quiet urban observation — interior light, neighborhood stillness, domestic moments — drawn from a daily watercolor diary I have maintained since 2020. My first solo illustration collection, Colour Diary, published in October 2021, grew directly from that practice and reflects the intimate, transparent quality I bring to every piece. More recently, I exhibited in Tide from China, a group show of Chinese illustrators held at ACG_Labo in Harajuku in February 2023, which marked my first formal exhibition presence in Japan. A representative selection of my work can be viewed on Instagram at @gegyjiji, and I would be glad to provide any additional materials your committee requires for review. I would be grateful to learn more about the submission process and to confirm whether my work would be appropriate for consideration before the June 11 deadline.

Sincerely,
GEGYjiji

GEGYjiji

Subject: Submission Inquiry — Laugh & Peace Art Competition 2026

Dear Laugh & Peace Art Competition team,

I am writing to inquire about submitting work to the Laugh & Peace Art Competition 2026, an open exhibition format that I believe is well suited to the kind of quiet, observational illustration I make. I am GEGYjiji, a Chinese watercolor artist based in Tokyo, and my practice centers on urban stillness, domestic interiors, and the texture of everyday light — subjects I developed through a daily watercolor diary I have kept since 2020. In 2021 I published my first solo illustration collection, Colour Diary, which gathered that diary work into a book and established the intimate, atmospheric voice that continues to define my pieces. More recently I participated in Tide from China Part 1, a group exhibition at ACG_Labo in Harajuku bringing together six Chinese illustrators working in Japan, which expanded my exhibition experience in the Tokyo area. I would welcome the opportunity to bring this body of work to an Osaka audience, and a full portfolio is available on Instagram at @gegyjiji. Could you please share details on the submission process, applicable fees, and the current deadline, as this information does not appear to be listed publicly?

Sincerely,
GEGYjiji
